topics.topic: Mapping customer references from a lost import to those minted by the repeated import
questions: How does the owner translate a governance entry that names a lost import's minted `customer_ref` to the replacement `customer_ref` minted by the repeated import?
How can an action recorded against a `customer_ref` minted by the lost import be matched to the different `customer_ref` minted by the repeated import?

quotes:
What the owner repeats after a restore — erasures,
restrictions, ends of a relationship, the greatest date audit entries were
ever erased by — follows the owner's record of the retention review (R0-60): a
governance document, outside this case (Explicit exclusions), naming each
action by its date, kind and the `customer_ref` or `project_id` it touched —
an audit erasure by its date alone — with no personal value.

The kept export and the import's choices hold
personal data — the import's choices include the names, kinds and tax-id
answers given for the Customers it made, each with the v1 `customer_ref` it
came from: the owner keeps them in the vault,
the owner's Bitwarden that only the owner reaches (R0-23), from the export's
making until their deletion; the governance
lists them as a copy that remains, as R0-81 lists the services' copies, and
the owner deletes them once a checked backup holds the import.

A repeated import mints new
`customer_ref`s for the Customers it makes; a consumer that kept one the lost
import minted relinks it in its own service, as R0-79 says for ids
production does not hold.

Each new
   Customer's `customer_ref` is minted when the import is accepted.
judgement.divergence: One recovery records or reconstructs a mapping from each lost minted `customer_ref` through its v1 value to the replacement reference and reapplies the recorded action to the intended Customer; another has only the lost reference and either skips the action or applies it to a guessed Customer. The owner and any service or customer affected by the missing restriction, erasure or relationship-end state notice.
judgement.why: The preserved choices identify Customers by their v1 values, while retention entries identify them only by the lost minted references, and no promised action or stored mapping connects those identities.

topics.topic: Recording and ordering reversible retention actions for recovery replay
questions: Does the record include restriction lifts and relationship resumptions as kinds, what date is recorded for an ended relationship—the action date or its effective end date—and how are multiple actions on the same day ordered for replay?
Must the record also preserve and replay inverse actions such as lifting a restriction and resuming a relationship, and if several actions affected the same record, in what order are they replayed?

quotes:
What the owner repeats after a restore — erasures,
restrictions, ends of a relationship, the greatest date audit entries were
ever erased by — follows the owner's record of the retention review (R0-60): a
governance document, outside this case (Explicit exclusions), naming each
action by its date, kind and the `customer_ref` or `project_id` it touched —
an audit erasure by its date alone — with no personal value.

Ending a customer relationship records the date the owner gives — the day the
relationship in fact ended, which may be earlier than the action — or today when
the owner gives none.

Until its record is deleted the owner may
resume the relationship; its deletion date is then reconsidered for the new
purpose of processing.

The owner restricts a customer's processing and may lift the restriction where
a lawful ground allows it.

The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so
   no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to
   the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for
   it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — and erases audit entries before
   the greatest date the owner ever erased by, before configuring the tokens and
   starting it again.
judgement.divergence: One recovery record includes lifts and resumptions, preserves the relationship's effective end date, and resolves actions into the current state before reopening; another records only the listed forward actions or replays same-day entries in an arbitrary order and uses the action date as the end date. The owner, Registry readers, and the retention review notice different restriction and relationship states or retention dates.
judgement.why: The texts require restoration to the current state but do not say whether inverse actions are recorded, which date represents an ended relationship, or how conflicting same-day entries determine that state.

topics.topic: Defining the interval of changes lost when restoring a backup
questions: Which changes are lost on restore: every change made after the restored backup was created and before the store loss, or some other interval?

topics.topic: Meaning of the recorded date for an audit erasure
questions: For an audit erasure, does “its date” mean the date the action occurred or the cutoff supplied to “erase audit entries before a date”?

topics.topic: Replaying a project erasure when the restored state lacks the prerequisite archive action
questions: How can the owner repeat an archived-project erasure when the restored backup predates the project's archive action and the governance record does not record that archive action?

topics.topic: Required customer identity choices and validation during project import
questions: When does the owner give these Customer choices, for which imported source records are they required, what values may a “tax-id answer” take, and what missing or invalid choice refuses the import?

topics.topic: Whether vault-held migration material is an exception to the one-home rule
questions: Is this vault-held migration material a temporary exception to R0-80, which says personal data is held only by Registry and admits only issued documents and Client Portal's offline projection as kept copies?
